title: Presidential Scholarship
program_type: University merit scholarship awarded at admission
funding_type: Tuition, housing and meal plan covered (university-funded merit award)
administering_authority: Clark University — Office of Financial Assistance and Office of Undergraduate Admissions
implementing_agency: Clark University — Office of Financial Assistance and Office of Undergraduate Admissions (same body)
programme_action: Clark University merit scholarship portfolio — Presidential Scholarship, historically associated with the LEEP Scholars programme (Liberal Education and Effective Practice); Clark's current undergraduate model is branded 'The Clark Experience'
description: The Presidential Scholarship is Clark University's most prestigious merit scholarship for first-year undergraduate students. It covers full undergraduate tuition plus on-campus housing and meals for all four years of study, regardless of the family's financial situation. Approximately five awards are made each year, and recipients are responsible for additional costs of roughly $12,000 to $15,000 per year. Consideration is tied to the undergraduate admissions application, and finalists are invited to interview.

programme_structure.award_types_detail: Clark publishes a single Presidential Scholarship tier. International first-year applicants are eligible for four further merit scholarships (International Traina, International Achievement, International Jonas Clark and Global Scholars), of which only the Presidential Scholarship is documented as covering tuition, housing and meals. International transfer students are eligible for only three merit scholarships (International Traina, International Achievement, International Jonas Clark), so the Presidential Scholarship is a first-year award only.
programme_structure.renewal_criteria: Clark's official pages state that the scholarship covers tuition, on-campus housing and meals for all four years. The specific renewal conditions (for example a minimum grade point average or continued full-time enrolment) are not stated on the current official pages and must be confirmed with the Office of Financial Assistance.
programme_structure.application_required: Official pages conflict. The Scholarships page and the Cost and Financial Aid page state there is no separate application process and that all admitted students are considered by the scholarship committee on the strength of the admissions application. The International Students financial assistance FAQ states that separate essays are required to be considered for the Presidential Scholarship. Clark also states that students must apply by the admissions deadline to be considered.

status_label: Open — admissions rounds for the next intake are accepting applications
status_note: Recurring annual cycle. Clark's published admissions deadlines are 1 November for Early Decision I and Early Action, and 15 January for Early Decision II and Regular Decision, so the current cycle is still open as of verification. Consideration for this award is tied to the admissions deadline. Clark publishes month/day deadlines without a year, so the record does not carry an exact year-stamped deadline.
verified_by: ScholarZone research agent — official clarku.edu source deep research
verification_notes: Verified directly against live Clark University pages on clarku.edu: the Scholarships page under Undergraduate Financial Assistance, the Cost and Financial Aid page under Undergraduate Admissions, the International Students page under Undergraduate Admissions, the International Students FAQ and hub pages under Undergraduate Financial Assistance, and the Apply, Application process and Early Decision pages. Benefit package, award count, eligibility, English proficiency indicators, application method and the applicant's residual cost responsibility are all confirmed. Two items could not be confirmed on any live official page: (1) a separate essay deadline for the scholarship (the official page that carried the scholarship essay process now redirects to the general financial aid page), and (2) a published total dollar value for the award. Aggregator sites such as crispng.com, admission.ac, eduspur.com, scholarshipregion.com, oyaop.com and unigo.com were consulted only to identify claims that needed official checking and were not used as sources for any field.

application_deadline.typical_application_window: Common Application and Coalition Application with Scoir open each year from around 1 August for the following fall entry. Round deadlines published by Clark: Early Decision I — 1 November; Early Action — 1 November; Early Decision II — 15 January; Regular Decision — 15 January. For the cycle reviewed here these correspond to 2026-11-01 (ED I and Early Action) and 2027-01-15 (ED II and Regular Decision).
application_deadline.application_period: Opens 1 August with the Common Application cycle; closes 1 November for Early Decision I and Early Action, and 15 January for Early Decision II and Regular Decision.
application_deadline.official_rule: Clark publishes only month and day, not a year. The official Cost and Financial Aid page states: 'Students must apply by the admissions deadline to be considered for the Presidential Scholarship.' The official Apply and Application process pages list: Early Decision I — November 1; Early Action — November 1; Early Decision II — January 15; Regular Decision — January 15. Because Clark publishes a recurring month/day rather than a dated deadline for this cycle, deadline_date is left null rather than inferred.
application_deadline.deadline_warning: Clark's live official pages contain no separate scholarship essay deadline and two official pages state there is no separate application process, while the International Students financial assistance FAQ states that separate essays are required for consideration. Aggregator sites repeatedly claim that the scholarship essays are due 1 November for Early Decision I and Early Action applicants and 1 February for Early Decision II and Regular Decision applicants; neither date appears on any live clarku.edu page and must be re-confirmed with the Office of Financial Assistance before being relied upon.

programme_duration.official_range: Four years of undergraduate study; the award covers all four years
programme_duration.renewal_note: Clark states the scholarship covers tuition, on-campus housing and meals for all four years. Months are not stated, so duration_months is null. Renewal conditions are not published on the current official pages.

funding.scholarship_type: Institutional full-cost merit award (tuition, on-campus housing and meal plan)
funding.monthly_amount_note: Clark awards no cash stipend. Housing and meals are provided in kind for all four years, so no monthly amount is published.
funding.travel_amount_note: No travel, installation, insurance or living allowance is published. Clark's official 2026-2027 cost of attendance lists a $250 transportation allowance, $900 estimated books and $800 estimated miscellaneous as student expenses, and a $2,833 health insurance cost that is not part of the award.
funding.institutional_costs: Full undergraduate tuition plus on-campus housing and meals for all four years are covered by the award. Clark's published 2026-2027 charges are tuition $62,070, room (standard double) $8,580 and board (standard plan) $5,780, with total billed charges of $77,970 which also include a $460 student activity and programming fee, a $400 orientation fee and a $680 health and wellness fee.
funding.fully_funded_note: Clark does not describe the award as fully funded. The official International Students page states that recipients are responsible for additional costs totalling approximately $12,000-$15,000 per year, and the official cost of attendance for 2026-2027 lists total estimated costs of $82,753 per year.

tuition.conditions: Full undergraduate tuition covered for all four years. $62,070 is Clark's published 2026-2027 tuition rate, cited as the cost of attendance the award covers; Clark does not publish an award value in dollars.
tuition.note: Covered in full for four years, regardless of family financial situation.

accommodation_support.conditions: On-campus housing covered. $8,580 is Clark's published 2026-2027 standard double room charge, cited as the cost of attendance the award covers.
accommodation_support.note: Covered for all four years (on-campus housing).

meal_plan_support.conditions: Meals covered. $5,780 is Clark's published 2026-2027 standard board plan charge, cited as the cost of attendance the award covers.
meal_plan_support.note: Covered for all four years (on-campus meals).

insurance.note: Not published in official source. Clark requires full-time students to participate in the Student Health Insurance Plan (published at $2,833 for 2026-2027) unless comparable U.S.-filed coverage is proven; this cost is not part of the award.

book_allowance.note: Not published in official source. Clark lists an estimated $900 per year for books as a student expense.

bond.note: No service or repayment bond is published for this award.

total_estimated_value.note: Clark does not publish a total dollar value for the Presidential Scholarship, and no total has been computed here. Published 2026-2027 costs of attendance that the award covers are tuition $62,070, room $8,580 and board $5,780.

Applicants who are not applying for transfer admission (transfer applicants are eligible for three other merit scholarships only)
Applicants with a strong secondary school record and demonstrated leadership potential
Applicants who submit an admission application by the Early Decision I, Early Action, Early Decision II or Regular Decision deadline

final_year_condition: For this undergraduate award the equivalent requirement is final-year secondary school completion: applicants must be first-year applicants who have completed at least the last three years of secondary education. Clark accepts applications in the final year of secondary school for fall entry.
equivalent_degree_note: International secondary school qualifications are accepted. Clark requires transcripts covering the last three years of education (with an extra transcript for systems such as China's 6-3-3) and grants advanced standing credit for Advanced Placement, British A-Level, International Baccalaureate, Ontario 13th Year, Quebec CEGEP, German Abitur, Swiss Matura, Italian Maturita, French or Moroccan Baccalaureate and CAPE Diploma.

eligibility.citizenship: Open to applicants of all citizenships. Clark's International Students page defines an international student as someone who does not hold U.S. citizenship or U.S. permanent residency, and states that all undergraduate admitted students, regardless of citizenship, are automatically considered for merit scholarships.
eligibility.residence_requirement: No residence requirement for the scholarship itself. All international applicants must complete Clark's International Student Certification of Finances and Financial Assistance Application Form after applying.
eligibility.secondary_school_requirement: Completion of secondary school is required. Clark requires transcripts covering the last three years of education, and classifies applicants as first-year (not transfer) students.
eligibility.academic_requirements: Clark states the award recognises outstanding academic achievements and leadership potential, placing recipients among the top applicants to Clark. No specific grade point average, class rank or percentage threshold is published for the scholarship. The admitted first-year class profile published by Clark is average high school GPA 3.68, mid-50% SAT 1300-1440 and mid-50% ACT 29-33, which is a class profile and not a scholarship threshold.
eligibility.language_requirement: If English is not the applicant's native language, an official TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo or Pearson PTE score report is required. Clark states it has no specific minimum scores but publishes general indicators; proficiency is assessed holistically with transcript, essay and letters of recommendation.
eligibility.extracurricular_requirement: Not a stated requirement. Clark's application review considers involvement in family, community and school activities beyond the classroom.
eligibility.leadership_requirement: Leadership potential is an officially cited criterion for the award.
eligibility.financial_need: Merit decisions are made without consideration of financial need. However, applicants must still document the ability to cover the costs the award does not cover, and Clark states it cannot offer admission to international students who require full funding. Clark describes its admissions process as need-aware for international applicants.
eligibility.previous_scholarship_restriction: No restriction on applicants who have held another scholarship is published.
eligibility.enrolment_status_requirement: First-year (not transfer) undergraduate enrolment at Clark University. Recipients must be admitted and enrol to receive the award.
eligibility.field_restrictions: None. The award is not restricted by major or discipline.

academic_requirements.percentage_note: No percentage, grade point average, class rank or standardised score threshold is published for the Presidential Scholarship. Clark is test-optional and states that test scores are not factored into merit aid decisions.
academic_requirements.programme_specific_requirements: Clark's International Students financial assistance FAQ states that separate essays are required to be considered for the Presidential Scholarship. Clark's Scholarships and Cost and Financial Aid pages state there is no separate application process and that consideration is based on the strength of the admissions application.
selection_factors_may_include: Strength of the admissions application (transcript, essays, recommendations, involvement)
Separate scholarship essays, per the International Students financial assistance FAQ
academic_requirements.holistic_selection_note: Clark reviews applications through a whole-person process, reading transcripts in full and considering academic challenge, growth over time, involvement beyond the classroom and letters of recommendation.

english_requirement.test_score_note: Clark states it does not have specific minimum scores and that the published figures are general indicators of the minimum English proficiency for studying at Clark; meeting them does not guarantee admission. Official test scores are preferred directly from the testing agency, although scanned copies from the applicant, counsellor or teacher are accepted for TOEFL, IELTS and PTE. Duolingo scores must come directly from the Duolingo portal. An interview may be used as a supplementary measurement of English proficiency. TOEFL is also published as 4.5 overall with no sub-score below 4 on the new scoring scale in force from January 2026, or 85 overall with no sub-score below 20. PEXT is published at 71 overall with no sub-score below 65.

language_of_instruction.language_note: Clark University is an English-medium institution in Worcester, Massachusetts. Clark's American Language and Culture Institute offers English for Academic Success for admitted applicants who may benefit from additional language support before or alongside degree coursework.

application_method.application_route: Submit one first-year undergraduate admission application to Clark through the Common Application or the Coalition Application with Scoir. Clark states all applicants are automatically considered for merit scholarships, while its International Students financial assistance FAQ states separate essays are required for Presidential Scholarship consideration. Applicants should confirm the current essay requirement and its deadline with the Office of Financial Assistance.
application_steps: Create a Common Application or Coalition Application with Scoir account (only one application may be submitted).
Apply to Clark University as a first-year applicant by the Early Decision I, Early Action, Early Decision II or Regular Decision deadline.
Indicate interest in the Presidential Scholarship where the application offers the option, so the applicant receives the essay instructions if they are required.
Submit transcripts covering the last three years of education, two letters of recommendation and, if English is not the native language, an official English proficiency score report.
Complete the International Student Certification of Finances and Financial Assistance Application Form, which becomes available on the applicant status portal after applying.
Complete any scholarship essays if requested by the Office of Financial Assistance.
Attend the finalist interview if invited.
application_method.application_fee: $0 — Clark charges no application fee for either the Common Application or the Coalition Application with Scoir route.

possible_awards: Clark University undergraduate degree (Clark's degree programmes are published at clarku.edu/programs; the pages read for this record do not enumerate the individual award titles)
degree_outcome.degree_note: Clark's official pages confirm the scholarship covers four years of undergraduate study. Clark's 2013 announcement of the LEEP Scholarship programme stated that recipients also received the opportunity to complete a master's degree tuition free through Clark's Accelerated B.A./Master's Degree Program; that benefit does not appear on the current Presidential Scholarship pages and should not be assumed for the current cycle.
degree_outcome.credit_transfer: Advanced standing credit is granted for qualifying pre-enrolment study, including Advanced Placement, British A-Level and International Baccalaureate, plus Ontario 13th Year, Quebec CEGEP, German Abitur, Swiss Matura, Italian Maturita, French or Moroccan Baccalaureate and CAPE Diploma. First-year students may be awarded a maximum of eight units of credit (two semesters) for AP credit and college work completed while in high school.

student_rights_and_cost_protection.tuition_fee_for_recipients: Full undergraduate tuition is covered for all four years, regardless of family financial situation. On-campus housing and meals are covered as well.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.application_fee_for_recipients: $0. Clark charges no application fee for the Common Application or the Coalition Application with Scoir, so receiving or not receiving the scholarship does not change it.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_breach_consequence: No bond or service obligation is published for this award.

practical_application_data.motivation_letter_strategy: Clark reads transcripts in full and values growth over time, particularly in the final two years of secondary school, alongside involvement beyond the classroom and letters of recommendation. Any scholarship essays should therefore show sustained academic rigour, concrete leadership and community impact, and a specific reason for Clark rather than general statements of ambition. Because Clark assesses English proficiency holistically across the transcript, essay and recommendations, clearly written application essays matter beyond the scholarship itself.

risk_flags.risk: Clark's live official pages conflict on whether a separate scholarship application or essays are required
risk_flags.impact: Applicants who follow one official page may miss a required essay and become ineligible, or may waste effort submitting material that is not needed.
risk_flags.mitigation: Email finaid@clarku.edu and intadmissions@clarku.edu before the admissions deadline to confirm the current essay requirement and deadline in writing.

risk_flags.risk: The award does not cover the full cost of attendance
risk_flags.impact: Recipients must fund approximately $12,000-$15,000 per year in additional costs, and Clark's published 2026-2027 total estimated costs are $82,753 per year.
risk_flags.mitigation: Budget from the earliest stage using Clark's published cost of attendance, and confirm how the residual cost will be met before accepting an offer.

risk_flags.risk: Only about five awards are made each year
risk_flags.impact: The award is highly competitive and cannot be relied on as a funding plan.
risk_flags.mitigation: Apply broadly and treat the other four international merit scholarships and any need-based aid as the realistic funding path.

risk_flags.risk: Clark's admissions process for international applicants is need-aware
risk_flags.impact: Clark states an application may be denied if the indicated financial need exceeds what it can provide through scholarships and aid, and that it cannot admit international students who require full funding.
risk_flags.mitigation: Present a credible and documented funding plan for the costs not covered, and avoid applying if full funding is required.

risk_flags.risk: The official page that documented the scholarship essay process and deadlines now redirects to the general financial aid page
risk_flags.impact: Process details such as essay topics, submission route and deadlines cannot be confirmed from live official pages and could change without notice.
risk_flags.mitigation: Re-verify with the Office of Financial Assistance at the start of each cycle; the record should be re-checked before the 1 November Early Decision I and Early Action deadline.

risk_flags.risk: Renewal conditions for years two to four are not published
risk_flags.impact: Recipients cannot confirm what academic standing is needed to keep tuition, housing and meals for four years.
risk_flags.mitigation: Request Clark's written renewal policy in the award letter and maintain full-time enrolment with strong grades.

risk_flags.risk: English proficiency figures are published as general indicators rather than guaranteed minimums
risk_flags.impact: An applicant meeting the published indicator scores is not guaranteed admission or scholarship consideration.
risk_flags.mitigation: Aim to exceed the published indicators, send official scores well before the deadline, and consider an interview, which can support the English assessment.

risk_flags.risk: No total dollar value is published for the award
risk_flags.impact: Third-party figures, including older quoted totals, may be outdated and cannot be treated as the award value.
risk_flags.mitigation: Use Clark's published 2026-2027 cost of attendance line items rather than any quoted scholarship total.

For the cycle reviewed, Early Decision I and Early Action fall on 2026-11-01 and Early Decision II and Regular Decision on 2027-01-15.

The commonly used phrase 'Clark University Presidential Scholarship (LEEP)' combines the award name with Clark's education model. LEEP (Liberal Education and Effective Practice) was launched in 2012 and, per Clark's official learning outcomes page, was replaced in 2025 by 'The Clark Experience'. Clark's 2013 article refers to 'the LEEP Scholarship' and links it to the scholarships page that now carries the Presidential Scholarship, so 'LEEP Scholarship' is recorded as a legacy title.
There is no widely used acronym or short form for this award, so short_title repeats the award name. LEEP is a model name, not a current acronym for the scholarship.

Clark publishes no total dollar value for the award, so total_estimated_value is marked unavailable and no total has been computed. The tuition, room and board figures quoted in funding_breakdown are Clark's published 2026-2027 cost of attendance line items, not an award value.
Official sources conflict on whether a separate application or essays are required. This is recorded rather than resolved, because both statements appear on live official clarku.edu pages.

Date fields (last_verified_at, last_verified_date, _verification_timestamp, logo_verified_at) use the verification date fixed by SCHEMA_CONTRACT.md, which states today is 2026-10-03. The pages cited were live and read for this record within that session.
No goal, cron or wakeup was used for this task; it was completed in a single research pass.
The record is not a fully funded award: Clark states recipients are responsible for additional costs of approximately $12,000-$15,000 per year.
